title: Operations Manager Salary Melbourne: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Convert an operations manager salary Melbourne to annual, fortnightly, and hourly pay. Use the 38-hour week, tax, and super calculator.
salarySummary: For a full-time operations manager in Melbourne, the ABS average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026) equates to about $108,352 annually based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for an operations manager role in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $50/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use the calculator on [the timesheet](/) to try different rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for operations managers?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). However, operations managers are usually covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Check the relevant award via [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include superannuation and tax for an operations manager salary Melbourne?
faqs.a: Yes. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold and a 2% Medicare levy. The result is an estimate; your actual tax may vary. See [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the hourly-to-annual conversion

When you're evaluating an **operations manager salary Melbourne**, the most reliable method is to start with your hourly rate and multiply it by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. The formula is simple:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as this is the ordinary hours under many modern awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work 38 hours, your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For example, at $50 per hour:

- Weekly: $50 × 38 = $1,900
- Fortnightly: $1,900 × 2 = $3,800
- Annual: $1,900 × 52 = $98,800

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It's a baseline estimate.

### The 38-hour week and the fortnight

Australia's full-time standard is 38 hours per week, as reflected in the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database. When you use the calculator on [the timesheet](/), you can enter your hourly rate and the hours per week. The tool then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures. The fortnight is particularly useful for budgeting if you're paid every two weeks.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates vs market rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, an **operations manager salary Melbourne** is almost always higher than the minimum. Most operations managers are covered by a modern award—such as the Business Equipment Award or the Professional Employees Award—or by an enterprise agreement. These instruments set minimum pay rates for each classification level.

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) that summarise the minimum rates for each award. For the most precise data, the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides spreadsheets with classifications, wage-related allowances, and penalty rates. The database is updated after each Annual Wage Review, most recently on 1 July 2026.

Beyond award minimums, market rates for operations managers in Melbourne vary by industry, experience, and company size. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings report (May 2026) shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week nationally. That equates to approximately $108,352 per year for a 38-hour week. This figure is a useful benchmark, but your actual salary may differ.

### Casual loading and superannuation

If you are employed casually, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base award rate. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add this loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading**—the tool will add it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12%, applied to your ordinary time earnings (excluding overtime). The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. So if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer contributes an extra $12,000 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare

Your gross annual pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) to see an estimate after tax and Medicare.

### Using the calculator for an operations manager salary Melbourne

To get a personalised estimate, start with your base hourly rate (or the rate you're offered). If you're comparing job offers, use the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page to see how different rates stack up. Remember that the calculator provides an estimate only—your actual pay and tax depend on your specific circumstances, including any allowances, penalty rates, or enterprise agreements.

For a quick reference, the [reference tables](/data) show common conversions. And if you want to check the minimum wage for your classification, visit [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage). The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT) can also give you award-specific pay rates, but note the disclaimer that the award prevails if there is any inconsistency.

In summary, converting an **operations manager salary Melbourne** from hourly to annual is straightforward with the 38-hour week formula. Use the ABS average weekly earnings as a market benchmark, but always check your award or agreement for the legal minimum. The calculator on this site will help you see the full picture: weekly, fortnightly, annual, super, and tax.
